questions.question: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

The second number in the given pair is a square of a number and the first number is a multiplied by 4 with the number of which the second number is a square of,

In other words: 4n : n²

**Now lets see the pairs,**

Option 1)12 : 9

3² = 9

3 × 4 = 12

Option 2) 8 : 4 

2² = 4

2 × 4 = 8

Option **3) 4 : 15**

**2² = 4 **

**4 × 4 = 16**

**Thus this option doesn't follow the same logic.**

Option4) 20 : 25

5² = 25

5 × 4 = 20

**Hence** , **it is very clear that option3) 4:15 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Seven friends L, M, N, O, P, Q and R, each has a different height. R is taller than L and shorter than Q. L is taller than M. N is the tallest among all. Only two people are taller than Q. O is not the shortest among all. Only one person is shorter than M. How many people are taller than R?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Seven friends: L, M, N, O, P, Q and R.

1. N is the tallest among all.

N > __ > __ > __ > __ > __ > __

2. Only one person is shorter than M.

N > __ > __ > __ > __ > M > __

3. Only two people are taller than Q.

N > __ > Q > __ > __ > M > __

4. L is taller than M.

N > __ > Q > __ > L > M > __

5. R is taller than L and shorter than Q.

N > __ > Q > R > L > M > __

6. O is not the shortest among all.

N > O > Q > R > L > M > __

The remaining place is for P.

N > O > Q > R > L > M > P

the final order will be ⇒ N > O > Q > R > L > M > P 

So,** 3** persons are taller than R.

Hence, the correct answer is **"3"**.

questions.question:
Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. 

**Statements: **

All reds are roses. 

No violet is red. 

Some tulips are violets. 

**Conclusions: **

I. Some roses are violets. 

II. No tulip is a red. 

III. No rose is a tulip.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/83fbcad9d56921203ad2af0b6e072a23572fbf1c3f7ead48095a949ca7395847.png] 

Conclusions: 

I. Some roses are violets. → False (There is no relation between roses and violets, therefore conclusion I is incorrect.)

II. No tulip is a red.→False (Tulips and red also has no relation, therefore conclusion II is also incorrect.)

III. No rose is a tulip. → False (As there is no definite negative relation given between them, definite negative conclusion will also be false.)

None of the conclusion follows here.

Hence, the correct answer is **"None of the conclusion follows".**

questions.question: If the 12th February 2011 was a Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 13th February 2015?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

On 12th February 2011 = Saturday

 12th February 2012 = Sunday

If a leap year comes immediately after an ordinary year, then the day on a certain date of the leap year will be 1 days ahead of the same date on the ordinary year upto February.

 12th February 2013 = Tuesday

If a leap year comes immediately after an ordinar
y year, then the day on a certain date of the leap year will be 2 days ahead of the same date on the ordinary year from March to December.

In any two consecutive ordinary years, date of the next year will be one day ahead of the same date of the previous year

 12th February 2014 = Wednesday

 12th February 2015 = Thursday 

 13th February 2015 = Friday (13th February comes just after 12th February)

Hence, the correct answer is** Friday.**

questions.question: If 01 February 2011 was Tuesday, then what was the day of the week on 01 January 2012?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

01 February 2011 = Tuesday

01 February 2012 = Wednesday

If a leap year comes immediately after an ordinary year, then the day on a certain date of the leap year will be 1 days ahead of the same date on the ordinary year upto February.

01 January 2012 is 31 days before 01 February 2012. (31 = 4 × 7 + 3 , 3 = odd days)

Number of odds days = 3 days

01 January = Sunday (three days before Wednesday)

Hence, the correct answer is **Sunday.**
